verdict: NOT READY TO MERGE - critical: C1
strengths: Every new test is behavioral. The strap_api tests drive the real record_run/run_tree/tree_name against an activated throwaway project, and the driver tests run strap.py in-process against a git repo. Nothing is stubbed.
test_record_run_redacts_machine_paths_before_hashing pins the hash-after-redaction order by recomputing sha256 over the stored reply, so redacting after hashing would fail it.

The redact_paths parametrization covers the realistic spellings an agent reply carries: POSIX, single and JSON-doubled backslashes, drive-letter case and Git Bash /c/. It also has negative tests for a longer sibling name (plan-red-1234567-2) and for case-sensitive POSIX matching.

test_record_run_keeps_machine_paths_out_of_the_spec checks the raw spec text, including the JSON-escaped backslash form, not just the parsed reply. That catches a path leaking through any field, not only Run.reply.

test_run_tree_keeps_an_absolute_tree keeps legacy specs with absolute Run.tree values working, and test_record_run_stores_reply_and_drops_tree still proves the driver resolves the now-relative tree when it removes it.

The arc-help-pages syntax test asserts the exact three code lines and that neither the native nor the POSIX project root appears in the section. The golden page update keeps the byte-identical-anywhere contract pinned with the new import line.
One helper (_tree / sa.run_tree) replaces every scattered Path(run.tree) in strap.py, so the brief, the runner row, the rewrites and record-run all see the same resolved tree.
sa.tree_name runs inside _place's try block, so a tree outside the worktree root is dropped before the StrapError (a ValueError that main already catches) surfaces.
Older specs keep working: pathlib's join drops the root before an absolute Run.tree, which the run_tree docstring states.

redact_paths replaces the longest path first and matches both separator spellings and the Git Bash /c/ form, so the tree keeps <tree> instead of becoming <worktree_root>/... and replies from either shell are covered.
The reply hash is computed on the redacted text, so the Run validator's reply_sha256 check still holds for the stored reply.
arc-help-pages names the archive by file name only, with a <folder> stand-in, and escapes the code block with quote=False, so the page stays free of paths and byte-identical at any root.
The v0.7.1 version table matches the tags: harness 0.65.1 at v0.7.0 to 0.65.3, and arc-straps 0.3.0 to 0.3.1, both as in plugin.json. arc-straps also moved out of the Unchanged list.

The strap-skills release note matches the code: `_machine_paths` maps the run tree, worktree root, project root and home folder to `<tree>`, `<worktree_root>`, `<project>` and `~` before the sha256, and `run_tree` keeps the old absolute trees working.

The SKILL.md build paragraph matches `_syntax_code` and `_syntax_section` line by line: import, ImportToolbox with the `<folder>` stand-in and the bare archive file name, the braced call, the alias note, then the derived outputs.

SKILL.md (lines 40-45), the arc-straps README and the release note all describe the same block the code emits: import arcpy, ImportToolbox with a <folder> stand-in, the call with braced optionals, the alias note, then derived outputs.
`ToolDoc.archive` is filled from `p.atbx.name` only, so the page keeps its no-path, byte-identical-at-any-root contract; the build module docstring stays true.
`_syntax_code` escapes the whole block with quote=False, so the <folder> placeholder renders as text and the raw-string quotes stay literal; the golden test pins the exact output.
Splitting the code block into `_syntax_code` keeps both functions short and gives each a docstring that matches its behavior; the models and source docstrings were updated alongside the new field.
arc-straps plugin.json bumped 0.3.0 -> 0.3.1 and the release table updated to match.
`_place` moved `tree_name` inside the try, so a tree outside the worktree root is dropped instead of left on disk after the refusal.
`run_tree` joins with `/`, so a legacy absolute `Run.tree` resolves unchanged. Old open runs still record, and recorded replies keep their pinned hashes.
`_machine_paths` adds each path in both its raw and its resolved spelling, which catches symlink, junction and 8.3 short-name variants without special cases.
`redact_paths` substitutes through a lambda, so placeholders are never parsed as regex replacement escapes, and it replaces the longest path first so nested roots keep their own placeholder.
The hash is taken after redaction, so `Run`'s reply_sha256 validator still holds and the stored text is what gets pinned.
The new tests are behavioral end to end: the driver test pipes a real reply through `record-run` and scans the tracked spec file for every machine spelling, escaped backslash form included.
The TREE line of the runner row and the brief still carry the absolute resolved path, so the runner agent contract (`TREE` absolute) in strap-scenario-runner.md is unchanged.
arc-help-pages names the archive by file only, keeping the byte-identical-at-any-root promise, and the golden test plus a dedicated no-path assertion pin the result.

important.name: Reply checks now run on the redacted reply
important.summary:
cmd_record_run evaluates the scenario checks against recorded.reply, which record_run now stores after redact_paths. A reply_matches or reply_absent check therefore sees placeholders instead of what the runner wrote. A path-hygiene scenario (reply_absent with a target like '[A-Za-z]:[\\/]' or '\.config/harness') always holds after redaction, so a baseline that leaks the tree, project or home path reads as clean, and a check that matches the tree's folder name stops matching. Neither the strap.py module docstring (line 23: 'Store the reply read from stdin, evaluate the checks against the tree') nor the Run docstring says that checks see the redacted text.

Also (roast): `cmd_record_run` evaluates the scenario checks against `recorded.reply`, which is now the redacted text. A `regex in the reply` check (strap-skills SKILL.md:297) that targets a tree name, a drive path or the home folder now sees `<tree>`, `<project>`, `<worktree_root>` or `~` and stops matching. Such a check was never portable, but a spec author has no way to learn the rule: the strap-skills SKILL.md check guidance and the release note both stay silent about which text the regex sees.
fix: Evaluate the checks on the raw reply read from stdin (pass `reply` instead of `recorded.reply` to sr.evaluate_checks at strap.py:731-732), keep storing the redacted text, and note in the Run docstring that check results come from the reply before redaction.

Keep the checks on the redacted reply, but say so in the strap.py record-run docstring line and the strap-skills authoring guidance, naming the placeholders (<tree>, <worktree_root>, <project>, ~) that reply_* check targets must use.

Add a clause to the Checks row of plugins/harness/skills/strap-skills/SKILL.md (line 297) saying that a reply regex runs on the stored reply, with machine paths already replaced by `<tree>`, `<worktree_root>`, `<project>` and `~`, and mention it in the v0.7.1 strap-skills line.

The other bullets in this file and in v0.7.0.md lead with the PR number and put the issue in parentheses (`#253 ... (issue #246)`). The arc-help-pages bullet at line 26 has no number at all.

Also (docs): `_syntax_section` (arc_help_pages_build.py:171-183) now emits the `import arcpy` and `ImportToolbox` lines plus a note naming the archive file (`ToolDoc.archive = p.atbx.name`). Every page built under 0.3.0 therefore differs from a rebuild, so `check_help_page` reports `help_page_stale` for all of them until `apply_help(page, apply=True)` runs again. Renaming the `atbx` file also stales every page now. Neither the release note nor the SKILL.md build paragraph says so, and SKILL.md line 45 only promises byte-identity across checkout roots.

Also (docs): The title 'Fix(strap-skills): `Run.tree` and `record_run` machine paths' leaves out the arc-help-pages syntax fix and the arc-straps 0.3.1 bump that this PR also ships, and the body is empty. The release note at lines 26-29 is the only place that describes the second fix.

The new strap-skills entry starts with `#254`, which is the issue ("Strap recorder writes absolute machine paths into tracked SkillSpec rows"); this PR is #255. The arc-help-pages entry has no number at all, although it ships in the same PR.

Also (roast): The syntax section of every page now holds two more lines and a note, so `check_help_page` reports `help_page_stale` for every page a consuming project built before arc-straps 0.3.1, until the project rebuilds them. The release line says only that a rebuild stays byte-identical, which is true of the next rebuild and does not cover the first one after upgrading. minor.name: Redaction misses the main checkout and the plugin root
minor.summary:
The record_run docstring (strap_api.py:314-315) and the Run docstring (strap_models.py:335-336) promise that the tracked spec carries no local path, but _machine_paths covers only the run tree, the worktree root, cfg.project_root and the home folder. When strap runs from a linked worktree, project_root is that worktree (project.project_root prefers the cwd's top level), so the main checkout is not covered. The run tree's .git file points into <main>/.git/worktrees/..., and `git worktree list` prints <main>, so a runner reply can carry it unredacted. The same goes for a plugin root outside home and outside the project (`--plugin-dir`), which the brief's launcher line prints.

Also (roast): `_machine_paths` redacts the run tree, the worktree root, `cfg.project_root` and the home folder. When strap runs from a linked worktree, which is the normal flow under `worktree_root`, `project_root` is that worktree. The main checkout (`main_worktree(project_root)`) is then left out, and on a machine where it sits on a different drive from home (for example `E:/...` against `C:/Users/...`) a reply that names it is stored with the path in plain text. The new `Run` docstring states flatly that a tracked spec names no local path. The four roots are a best-effort list, and the most likely fifth root is missing.
fix: Add `("<main>", main_worktree(cfg.project_root))` (harness_lib.project) and the plugin root to the pairs in _machine_paths; the longest-first order keeps nested paths correct.
Narrow both docstrings to the paths actually replaced.

Add `("<project>", main_worktree(cfg.project_root))` to the pairs in `_machine_paths` (or give it its own placeholder such as `<main>`; longest-first ordering already keeps a worktree under it distinct), with a test that names the main checkout from a linked worktree.
Reword the `Run` docstring in strap_models.py so it lists the roots that are redacted instead of promising that no local path is named.

minor.name: Path pattern matches inside a dot-suffixed longer name
minor.summary:
The _path_pattern docstring says neither form matches inside a longer name, but the trailing lookahead is (?![\w-]) and leaves '.' out (the leading lookbehind includes it). So the path E:/a/operator-straps matches the front of E:/a/operator-straps.wiki/x and yields '<project>.wiki/x'. The '.' was likely left out on purpose so that sentence-ending punctuation still matches, but the docstring states the stricter rule.

Also (roast): `_path_pattern` guards the left edge with `(?<![\w.-])` but the right edge only with `(?![\w-])`, so a dot after the last segment still counts as a boundary. With home `C:/Users/dev`, the text `C:/Users/dev.old/x` becomes `~.old/x`. With the tree `.../plan-red-1234567`, the sibling `.../plan-red-1234567.bak/a.py` becomes `<tree>.bak/a.py` when `<worktree_root>/plan-red-1234567.bak/a.py` was correct. The docstring promises that neither form matches inside a longer name, and the recorded reply that judges quote from now says something the runner never wrote. The dot is probably allowed so that a sentence can end right after a path; that case can be kept without the false match. `test_redact_paths_leaves_a_longer_name_alone` tests only the `-2` suffix, so this gap is never exercised.
fix: Use the lookahead (?![\w-]|\.[\w-]) so a dot is allowed only when no name character follows it, which keeps the sentence-final period working.
Or reword the docstring: a path followed by a '.' suffix still matches.

Make the right guard `(?![\w-]|\.[\w-])` so a sentence-ending dot still matches but `.bak` or `.old` does not, and add a `.bak` case to `test_redact_paths_leaves_a_longer_name_alone` in tests/lib/test_strap_runs.py.

minor.name: No test covers the home-folder '~' placeholder that _machine_paths adds
minor.summary: strap_api._machine_paths (plugins/harness/lib/harness_lib/strap_api.py:301-308) redacts four roots: tree, worktree root, project and Path.home() as '~'. test_record_run_redacts_machine_paths_before_hashing checks the first three, but no reply names a path under home outside the other roots. Removing the home pair, or ordering it wrongly against a shorter project root, would still pass every test. On Windows tmp_path sits under the home folder, so the longest-first ordering is exercised only incidentally.
fix: In the rooted test, monkeypatch Path.home to return tmp_path / 'home' (two or more segments, so _path_pattern accepts it), add a reply line 'Home: <home>/notes.txt', and expect 'Home: ~/notes.txt' in the stored reply.
Add a separate strap_api test that calls record_run with a monkeypatched home and asserts the '~' substitution and the matching reply_sha256.

minor.name: test_strap_runs module docstring omits redact_paths

The docstring does not mention any of it.
fix: Add a clause before the import-boundary clause, e.g. '``redact_paths`` (every separator, case and ``/c/`` spelling of a drive path, longest path first, never inside a longer name, POSIX paths case-sensitive)'.
